free_tier.stated: A free 30-day trial with 3 domains, 900 records, unlimited queries during the trial, 1 failover record, 5 query logs, 2FA, DNS analytics and a 100% SLA; there is no perpetual free tier and paid plans start at USD 6.25 per month
free_tier.notes: the trial is time-boxed at 30 days rather than capacity-boxed; the 30-day length is the head-line allowance, so the unit names wall-clock time

per_object_cap.stated: 900 records across 3 domains on the trial and 7,500 records across 25 domains on the cheapest paid Business plan; no single-record size cap is stated
per_object_cap.notes: the cap is a record count, not a byte size

retention.stated: the trial ends after 30 days, after which a paid plan is required to keep the zones active; no separate retention window for zones on a paid plan was read
retention.notes: 30 days is the trial length, which is the clock that decides access to the offer

egress.terms: unlimited DNS queries during the 30-day trial; on the paid Business plan 10M queries per month are included and overages are invoiced

interface_detail: a REST API at https://api.dnsmadeeasy.com/V2.0/ using x-dnsme-apiKey, x-dnsme-requestDate and an HMAC-SHA1 x-dnsme-hmac header; a separate dynamic DNS update servlet at https://cp.dnsmadeeasy.com/servlet/updateip takes username, password, record id and ip. The API reference documents full record and domain CRUD, secondary DNS, failover and query-usage calls
tooling: curl with the x-dnsme-* HMAC headers, the sample dnsmeapi.pl Perl wrapper, and dynamic DNS clients such as ddclient; public SDKs and terraform providers exist from third parties
chaining: a managed authoritative DNS service that can serve as a primary or secondary zone and can be paired with another DNS provider for redundancy; dynamic DNS clients update A records through the update servlet

limits.value: the free offer is a 30-day trial; a paid plan is required afterwards
3 domains and 900 records on the trial; 25 domains and 7,500 records on the paid Business plan
150 REST API requests per 5 minute scrolling window per API key
REST API keys are available only on Business / DNS-25 memberships or above; DNS-5 members must upgrade

binding_note: the free offer is only a 30-day trial, so the clock ends access before the record count, API rate or API-key gate binds for a free user; API access is also gated to paid tiers

identity_cost.detail: the trial signup guide lists username, password, confirm password, email, first name and last name, then company name, address, city, state, country, zip, phone, an optional fax, a secret question and secret answer, and an optional charity; no card is listed on the Create an Account page and Prerequisites is None, so no payment card is asked for at trial signup (https://support.dnsmadeeasy.com/hc/en-us/articles/34327085326107-How-to-Sign-Up-With-DNS-Made-Easy-Free-Trial). A phone number is requested as account information for the business

reliability_note: REST API calls with invalid credentials or an invalid request-date header receive HTTP 403, and calls arriving more than 30 seconds after the request-date and HMAC are generated are denied; an account suspended for complaints or misuse returns error-auth-suspend on a dynamic DNS update
confidence_note: the free-trial signup guide, the DigiCert first-party pricing blog, the API reference, the API-key article, the add-ons article and the dynamic DNS article were read and quoted; no signup form was submitted, so the exact fields are as documented rather than measured. The marketing pricing and free-trial pages at dnsmadeeasy.com now answer 404 or serve a DigiCert UltraDNS page, so the trial terms come from the support guide and the first-party DigiCert blog

The blog and the signup guide disagree on the trial record count (900 versus 1,500), so the lower guide figure is used.
